title: Canonical open and closed base-change mates for arbitrary ring sheaves
statement: Let X be qcqs, i:Z→X closed and j:U→X quasi-compact open with complementary ranges, and B an arbitrary ring object in abelian pro-etale sheaves. For every g:X′→X with X′ qcqs, the two fixed coefficient square comparison maps [def-sf-proetale-ring-sheaf-operations] are multiplicative. There exist module inverse-image square isomorphisms delta and gamma whose carriers are precisely the fixed comparisons, and natural isomorphisms alpha:g^*j_!≅j′_!g_U^* and beta:g^*i_*≅i′_*g_Z^*. The adjoint of alpha inverse is g_U^* of the open unit followed by delta inverse at j_!; the adjoint of beta is gamma at i_* followed by g_Z^* of the closed counit. No sequence exactness or compatibility with its two arrows is asserted here.

proof.text: For inverse-image composition, the conjugate of the monoidal direct-image composition comparison is monoidal, by isMonoidal_conjugateEquiv_symm. The monoidal adjunction and its composite supply the required structures. Congruence along equal scheme maps is monoidal by substitution. Consequently upperStarCompIso is monoidal. Its coefficient component is multiplicative; reconcile successive and composite MonObj structures with monObjObj_comp and IsMonHom.of_eq. Construct delta and gamma with NatIso.ofComponents and Mod.isoMk. Naturality and the monoidal tensor equation prove linearity, with exactly the prescribed underlying comparison.

Complementary exact restrictions jointly detect isomorphisms: the abelian supported-unit theorem detects zero objects, Mod.forget reflects zero, and exact inverse image transports kernels and cokernels. The open module unit is invertible by the carrier calculation and full faithfulness of abelian open extension.

The pulled-back immersions remain complementary, since their ranges are inverse images of the original ranges; the geometric base-change instances preserve their immersion and quasi-compactness hypotheses. Apply the proved closed-localization theorem on both schemes for the invertible closed counits and vanishing j^*i_*. Adjunction transposition also gives i^*j_!=0 on each scheme.

Define t:j′_!g_U^*→g^*j_! as the inverse adjunct of the pulled-back open unit followed by delta inverse. Naturality follows by transposing, using naturality of delta inverse and of the unit. Its closed restriction is a map between zero objects, by i^*j_!=0 and gamma. Its open restriction is invertible because its composite with the invertible open unit is the prescribed composite of isomorphisms. Joint detection makes t invertible. Set alpha to its inverse. Its transpose equation is Equiv.apply_symm_apply.

Define v:g^*i_*→i′_*g_Z^* as the adjunct of gamma followed by the pulled-back closed counit. Naturality follows by transposing and using naturality of gamma and the counit. Its open restriction is a map between zero objects. After closed restriction, its composite with the invertible closed counit is the prescribed composite of isomorphisms. Joint detection makes v invertible. Set beta=asIso v. Its transpose equation is Equiv.symm_apply_apply.

lean.statement:
theorem ringSheaf_baseChange_mates
    {X Z U : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X]
    (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : U ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsOpenImmersion j]
    [QuasiCompact j] (_hU : Set.range j = (Set.range i)ᶜ)
    (B : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}) [MonObj B] :
    (∀ {X' : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X'] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X'] (g : X' ⟶ X),
      Exists fun [_hu : IsMonHom (ringSheafSquareCoefficient g j B)] ↦
      Exists fun [_hz : IsMonHom (ringSheafSquareCoefficient g i B)] ↦
      ∃ delta : ringSheafInverseImage g B ⋙
            ringSheafInverseImage (pullback.fst g j) ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} g).obj B) ≅
          ringSheafInverseImage j B ⋙ ringSheafSquarePullback g j B,
      ∃ gamma : ringSheafInverseImage g B ⋙
            ringSheafInverseImage (pullback.fst g i) ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} g).obj B) ≅
          ringSheafInverseImage i B ⋙ ringSheafSquarePullback g i B,
        (∀ M, (delta.hom.app M).hom = (ringSheafSquareComparison g j).hom.app M.X) ∧
        (∀ M, (gamma.hom.app M).hom = (ringSheafSquareComparison g i).hom.app M.X) ∧
        ∃ alpha : ringSheafOpenExtension j B ⋙ ringSheafInverseImage g B ≅
            ringSheafSquarePullback g j B ⋙
              ringSheafOpenExtension (pullback.fst g j) ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} g).obj B),
        ∃ beta : ringSheafDirectImage i B ⋙ ringSheafInverseImage g B ≅
            ringSheafSquarePullback g i B ⋙
              ringSheafDirectImage (pullback.fst g i) ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} g).obj B),
          (∀ N, (ringSheafOpenAdjunction (pullback.fst g j)
                ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} g).obj B)).homEquiv _ _ (alpha.inv.app N) =
            (ringSheafSquarePullback g j B).map ((ringSheafOpenAdjunction j B).unit.app N) ≫
              delta.inv.app ((ringSheafOpenExtension j B).obj N)) ∧
          (∀ G, ((ringSheafAdjunction (pullback.fst g i)
                ((upperStar Ab.{u + 1} g).obj B)).homEquiv _ _).symm (beta.hom.app G) =
            gamma.hom.app ((ringSheafDirectImage i B).obj G) ≫
              (ringSheafSquarePullback g i B).map ((ringSheafAdjunction i B).counit.app G)))
